meta.intro: Nvidia got its CEO back on the White House's word, and the money that matters went to the edges: non-Nvidia inference, robot brains, and the trust layer between apps and models.
meta.briefingTitle: Huang Returns, and the Money Goes Around Nvidia
meta.summary: Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back 11 days after he resigned and said Washington had weighed in, so the stock's 33% bounce now comes with a political-risk premium. Underneath, capital is working around Nvidia: Accel's $277M seed for Marlowe's Etched-and-AMD inference sites, AMD's $2.9B Taalas buy, and a16z's $110M seed for Embo's world-model robots. The plumbing in between got riskier: OpenRouter found leaking providers and OpenAI now gatekeeps resellers. Japan's moves are smaller and more cautious: a first paid tender for domestic LLMs, a ¥45B buyout fund that installs AI in small firms, and SoftBank's $500M going to a German robot maker rather than a Japanese one.

gaps.label: Sovereign frontier-model pretraining
gaps.note: Unchanged. The Digital Agency's Gennai tender is the first time the government will pay for domestic LLMs, but PFN's new PLaMo 3.0 Fin still trails Qwen3.5-9B on finance knowledge. OpenAI says its frontier is now below 0.8 log-perplexity and is proposing a ceiling near 0.7, so the US is debating where to stop while Japan is still catching up.

gaps.label: Depth of private risk capital for AI infrastructure
gaps.note: Japan down 1. Japan's largest physical-AI check this week was SoftBank's $500M into Germany's Agile Robots. At home the money came through Sumitomo/REVA's ¥45B SME buyout fund, not VC. In the US, Accel put $277M into a six-month-old non-Nvidia inference company as a seed round.

gaps.label: Domestic leading-edge chip manufacturing
gaps.note: Unchanged. TSMC's Kumamoto Fab 2 is cleared for 3nm but starts at only ~6,000 wafers a month in Dec 2028, and Rapidus now guides to late 2027 or early 2028 for 2nm volume. The US frontier is moving to custom inference silicon: AMD bought Taalas for $2.9B and Marlowe runs on Etched.

gaps.label: Early-stage AI venture formation and exits
gaps.note: Unchanged. STRACT's ~¥1.2B Docomo-led round is a solid Japanese agent raise, about $9M. In the same week US seeds ran $110M (Embo) and $277M (Marlowe). Sakana says it has no near-term IPO plans, so Japan's flagship lab still has no exit timeline.

items.headline: Nvidia's Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO 11 Days After He Resigned, Citing 'Input From Senior Levels' of the US Government, and the Stock Jumps ~33%
items.dek: The key-person risk is back on Nvidia's books, and now there is a political-risk premium too.

analysis.happening: An 8-K filed Nov 23 says the board unanimously reinstated Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. He quit Nov 12; six days ago the chair said there was no plan to bring him back. CNBC put the rebound at ~33%, after the SOX fell ~17% in the week to Nov 20.
analysis.now: Few are quoting this part: the filing says outright that governance went through the White House, and that leverage can cut either way. Caveat: the SEC accounting questions reported last week are unresolved, so this is a relief rally, not a clean bill of health.
analysis.future: Watch for board departures or new governance commitments, any SEC update, and whether the bounce spreads to AMD, TSMC and memory or stays Nvidia-only. Analog Devices (Nov 24) and Dell later this week will show whether chip demand holds up apart from the drama.

items.headline: Six-Month-Old Marlowe Raises a $277M Seed at $1.15B, Led by Accel, to Run Inference on Etched and AMD Chips Instead of Nvidia's, as AMD Closes Its $2.9B Taalas Deal
items.dek: In the same week, investors and AMD both paid up for inference that doesn't run on CUDA.

analysis.happening: Marlowe was founded in May 2026 by Convoy co-founder Dan Lewis and ex-Microsoft AI leader Kutta Srinivasan. Accel led its $277M seed, with Bessemer, Altimeter and Atreides. Its first site goes live in December on Etched chips, with an AMD site in Q2 2027. AMD closed its ~$2.9B Taalas buy (~$1.4B contingent).
analysis.now: The thesis is that inference splits by workload, so someone has to schedule, compile and route across mixed silicon. That software gap is open. Caveat: Etched is unproven at scale, the site timelines come from a single outlet, and AMD's ~48% earn-out shows it is paying for milestones it hasn't seen yet.
analysis.future: Watch whether the December Etched site ships and what it charges per token compared with B200 clouds. Also watch whether MatX and other model-specific ASIC startups draw bids from Broadcom, Marvell or the hyperscalers now that exits have prices.

items.headline: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers and Pulls 'Zero Data Retention' From 125 Endpoints After a Canary Test Leaked Secrets, Days After OpenAI Began Requiring Approval for Any Reseller
items.dek: Both moves hit the model-router layer in the same week: one for leaks, the other for control.

analysis.happening: Dragos sent ~2M prompts seeded with decoy credentials through OpenRouter. At least three providers exposed data, and outsiders used some of the credentials. Separately, from Nov 20 OpenAI requires its sign-off for any service reselling direct model access. It has published no form, criteria or grandfathering.
analysis.now: A 'ZDR' badge on a cheap endpoint turns out to be a claim, not a guarantee. Rotate any secret that went through an affected route. Margin and control move from aggregators back to the labs. Caveat: the three providers weren't named, some delistings were precautionary, and no router has been cut off by OpenAI yet.
analysis.future: Expect continuous canary and attestation testing of inference providers to become a product, with TEE hosting sold as a premium tier. Watch whether Anthropic and Google copy OpenAI's rule. For builders, have a multi-provider fallback and use Bedrock or Azure as 'pre-approved' routes.

items.headline: OpenAI's Chief Scientist Proposes an Industry-Wide 'Perplexity Ceiling' and Publishes Internal Numbers: ~0.91 for GPT-4, Under 0.8 Now, With a 'Transformative' Band Near 0.68-0.70
items.dek: Pachocki wants labs to stop training past a shared loss threshold until AI-behavior monitoring reaches a set milestone.

analysis.happening: OpenAI disclosed log-perplexity on internal held-out data: ~0.99 for GPT-3.5, 0.91 for GPT-4, and below 0.8 for current frontier models. Jakub Pachocki puts the next 'transformative' band at ~0.68-0.70 and warns AI could start accelerating its own training as early as 2027. Altman called it the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while.
analysis.now: This is the first time a frontier lab has proposed one auditable number as a brake. It is also a way to shape what regulators measure. Caveat: the post sets no threshold or milestone and makes no binding commitment. Labs' datasets differ, and reasoning can add capability without lowering perplexity.
analysis.future: Watch whether Anthropic, Google or the AI safety institutes adopt a shared held-out corpus. Building and certifying that corpus is a neutral third-party business. If a 'monitoring milestone' shows up in procurement, CoT-monitoring and interpretability vendors gain.

items.headline: a16z Leads a $110M Seed in Embo, the Robot-Brain Startup From Danijar Hafner, Creator of DeepMind's Dreamer World Models, With Khosla, DST and NVentures
items.dek: Robotics labs built on world models now raise nine-figure seeds before shipping a product.

analysis.happening: Hafner announced the $110M seed on Nov 23. a16z led, with Khosla, DST Global, NVentures and Striker. CTO Wilson Yan created VideoGPT. The plan is to pretrain one model on internet-scale video, then fine-tune it and train it with RL on Embo's own humanoids. No valuation was disclosed.
analysis.now: The bet is that robots can 'rehearse in imagination' instead of relying on expensive teleop data, and Nvidia's venture arm joining fits its physical-AI push. Caveat: Embo is research-stage with no product, and The Information reported talks back in March, so the round took ~8 months to close.
analysis.future: Watch for first public benchmarks, the size of Embo's own robot fleet, and whether other world-model labs raise similar seeds. Tooling for robot RL data pipelines (sim-to-real evals, video curation) is an opening for builders.

items.headline: The Digital Agency's 'Gennai' Tender for Domestic LLMs, With a 300-Question Civil-Service Exam, Is Due This Month, the First Time Government Will Pay for Japanese Models
items.dek: Japan's sovereign-LLM effort is about to get its first real revenue test.

analysis.happening: The agency said the FY2027 call opens in November 2026. Document screening is in December, a 300-question test across 35 skills (up from 50) in January, the award in March and use from April. Models must run on Government Cloud and support tool calling. The first-round trialists were NTT Data, SoftBank, NEC, Fujitsu and PFN.
analysis.now: It's Japan's version of US GSA OneGov deals, but domestic-only, which shields bidders from GPT and Claude. Caveat: as of mid-November no call had been seen publicly, so timing may slip. The honest benchmark is PFN's new PLaMo 3.0 Fin, which scored below Qwen3.5-9B on finance knowledge in one test.
analysis.future: Watch whether Sakana, ELYZA/KDDI or Stockmark join the incumbents. The exam itself creates a market for eval harnesses, admin-domain fine-tuning data and tool-use wrappers that help smaller models pass, and those can be sold to every bidder.

items.headline: Sumitomo Backs REVA's ¥45B Buyout Fund to Buy 30-40 Small Japanese Firms and Install AI From the Inside
items.dek: A trading house is turning AI adoption into a private-equity play on Japan's aging, successor-less manufacturers.

analysis.happening: Nikkei reports Sumitomo Corp. and REVA, a Tokyo PE firm in which Sumitomo holds over 10%, formed a ~¥45B (~$290M) fund. It plans to invest in 30-40 SMEs over several years and bring Sumitomo's AI know-how to their factory operations. REVA's first fund, in 2023, was ~¥33B.
analysis.now: In the US, AI usually reaches SMEs as SaaS sold to owners. In Japan, many owners have no successor, so the route may be to buy the company and install the AI yourself. Caveat: Nikkei Asia says Sumitomo is putting in only 'several billion yen', and there's no official release yet.
analysis.future: Each roll-up needs repeatable tooling for messy plant data: OCR of paper records, PLC log ingestion, scheduling agents. A productized 'AI value-creation team' could be sold to every fund. Watch whether JIP, Advantage and other Japanese PE firms copy the model.

items.headline: SoftBank Leads a $500M Series F in Germany's Agile Robots at $8.5B, With Hitachi Joining, While Japan's Own Physical-AI Startups Raise ¥10M to ¥1.75B
items.dek: Japan's biggest physical-AI money keeps going abroad.

analysis.happening: Munich-based Agile Robots raised $500M at $8.5B. SoftBank Group led, with Nvidia, Hitachi, Hitachi Ventures and T.Capital. The money funds US expansion and a 10,000-humanoid-a-year German plant. Japan's domestic physical-AI rounds this month were MUSE at ¥1.75B and Kyutech spinout HPI at ¥10M via a JFC loan.
analysis.now: That is roughly a 30-40x gap in round size, in a sector where Japan leads on installed industrial robots. Caveat: these are different stages, and SoftBank's own shares fell ~16% on Nov 20, so this is not a sign of easy money at home.
analysis.future: Watch whether Agile Robots sets up a Japan entity or deploys with Hitachi on Japanese factory floors. The gap to build into: Japanese robot data, teleoperation and fleet integration, which foreign humanoid makers need in order to sell into Japanese plants.

items.headline: STRACT Raises ~¥1.2B, Led by NTT Docomo Ventures, for DONDO, a Shopping Agent Built for Rakuten, Amazon.co.jp and Yahoo Shopping
items.dek: Japan's agentic commerce is being built locally, not imported from OpenAI or Perplexity.

analysis.happening: STRACT announced ~¥1.2B (~$9.2M, per Dealroom) in equity plus debt on Nov 18. Docomo Ventures led, with Mizuho Capital, GMO VenturePartners, Headline and Delight Ventures. It has raised ¥2.62B in total. Its earlier app, PLUG, had 3M+ downloads and 800K MAU. The money goes to compute, the DONDO and ureteku AI products, and security.
analysis.now: In the US, frontier labs are building checkout agents themselves (ChatGPT Instant Checkout, Perplexity). Japan's fragmented marketplaces and points systems leave room for a local agent. Caveat: the round is small and partly debt, and the cost of compute per user could squeeze margins.
analysis.future: Watch whether Docomo puts DONDO in front of d POINT members, which would be real distribution. The unowned layer is merchant-side: agent-readable product feeds and inventory and returns APIs that let Japanese EC operators be bought by agents.
